qualification: Isolated Date grammar on the committed shared-VM baseline; other pending Date, host and Wasm changes excluded and preserved.

representation.grammar: One numeric form selection derives field widths and ISO fallback policy. Full/partial dates use the same omitted-field defaults; space forms admit the pinned legacy field/offset widths.
representation.construction: Date.parse and string construction use one parser and the shared date constructor. Offsets adjust the minute component before shared TimeClip, preserving valid range-boundary values.
representation.reduction: Removed standalone year parsing and chrono local-ISO reconstruction; fractional milliseconds are folded without padding-string allocations. Grammar widths, defaults and limits have named owners.

build.profile: release, correctness only; no performance claim

node_controls.scope: 73 strings in UTC, America/New_York and Asia/Kathmandu; normal/generic paths observe Date.parse and string construction. ISO/space field widths, partial/expanded years, fractional precision, offsets, date limits and DST transitions.

remaining_differences.dst_gap: Two New York inputs in both modes still return NaN because the shared local date conversion rejects nonexistent wall times. This is a concrete follow-up correctness gap, not a pass.
remaining_differences.negative_zero_year: The date-only -000000-01-01 input remains NaN in all three zones and both modes. Local Node accepts it through permissive parsing; Quench retains the ECMAScript invalid expanded-year rule. Strict negative-zero cases in the pinned suite pass.

units: No new general Date units duplicating suite cases. The selected production suites and matched oracle observations qualify this pure parsing change.
limits: The eight unchanged Date stress timeouts at the matched ten-second deadline remain failures. No fixture, helper, expectation or inventory changed.
Stage A, complete current Test262, Wasm and implemented Node qualification remain open.
